official_evidence.supported_syntax: transport_descriptor/interfaceWhiteList/address containing the local interface IPv4 address; documented for UDP and TCP transports
official_evidence.limits: This documents XML syntax only. The installed binary version, actual NIC availability and actual participant/profile loading were not tested here.

implementation: Optional run/CLI parameters windows_dds_interface and linux_dds_interface must be supplied together as IPv4 strings. Validation uses stdlib IPv4Address before any stage reads, file writes or process ownership setup.

With the pair, author fastdds-udp-windows.xml and fastdds-udp-linux.xml, each containing only its platform address in the UDP interfaceWhiteList. The SDK receives the Windows profile path; WSL receives the /mnt drive path for the Linux profile, via both existing Fast DDS environment variable names.

pair-host.json retains the previous ros_transport fields and adds interface_whitelist windows/linux address/profile/SHA records only when enabled. Both XML files and hashes are included in SDK job-spec expected_inputs.

With neither address, preserve the original fastdds-udp.xml content, environment and report schema. Existing UDP-only/useBuiltinTransports=false behavior, domain/QoS and physics/executor arguments remain unchanged. No runtime addresses are hardcoded.
root_usage: Append --windows-dds-interface <current-Windows-IPv4> --linux-dds-interface <current-Linux-IPv4> to the existing pair invocation. Omit both to retain the unscoped baseline. Root supplies verified current addresses.

validation.scope: Default profile/environment and overwrite refusal; independent XML addresses, actual run wiring with mocked external calls, platform paths and both report/input hashes; seven malformed or partial pairs rejected before files/processes. No actual SDK/WSL process was launched.
